passage: The rain clouds were dark and the auto was waiting at the market gate. “Ojas, hold my hand and walk to the auto,” said his aunt Jyoti, juggling two heavy bags. Ojas held on for four steps. Then a small brown puppy trotted out from under a cart, and Ojas let go. He crouched beside it, one finger stretched out. The first raindrops fell. “Ojas! The auto!” Jyoti called. Ojas looked up, blinking, as if he had forgotten there was an auto at all. Jyoti put down a bag, lifted him with one arm, and the puppy watched them go.

qa.q: Where was the auto waiting?
qa.a: The auto was waiting at the market gate.

qa.q: What was Ojas thinking about when Jyoti called about the auto?
qa.a: Ojas was absorbed in the puppy and delighted by it: he looked up, blinking, as if he had forgotten there was an auto at all.

qa.q: What could Jyoti do next time in a busy market?
qa.a: Hold Ojas's hand firmly, or give one clear job like “walk with me to the auto”, and steer away from small distractions like puppies.

qa.q: What is it like for Jyoti when Ojas lets go?
qa.a: Jyoti is hurried and juggling bags with rain coming, so probably feels anxious but patient, and lifts Ojas rather than scolding.

grounding: A young child sets out toward a goal, is pulled by a puppy and forgets the original goal.

passage: In the Mumbai flat, Ritu sat on the floor to put on her school shoes. Her big sister Sarita was waiting at the door with the bag. Ritu pushed her left foot into one shoe. Then she saw her toy bus under the sofa. She pulled it out and rolled it along the tiles. "Vroom." She drove it to the kitchen and back. The second shoe lay forgotten by the door. "Ritu! Shoes!" Sarita called. Ritu looked down, surprised to see one bare foot. Sarita put the bus on the shelf and held out the shoe.

qa.q: Which shoe did Ritu put on first?
qa.a: Ritu pushed her left foot into one shoe.

qa.q: Why did Ritu look surprised when Sarita called her?
qa.a: She had become so interested in the toy bus that she forgot her goal, and was genuinely surprised to see one bare foot.

qa.q: What worked about Sarita's response?
qa.a: Sarita put the bus out of sight and held out the shoe, which removed the distraction and gave Ritu back the task.

qa.q: What is it like for Sarita waiting at the door?
qa.a: Sarita is probably a bit impatient, standing with the bag ready while her little sister plays with the bus.

grounding: Shows a young child who starts putting on shoes and ends up playing with a toy, forgetting the original goal.

Yogesh: "Aadhya, brush your teeth, then story time."
Aadhya: "Okay, Papa!"
(She squeezes the paste. Then she spots the rubber duck on the tub's edge.)
Aadhya: "Papa, the duck is thirsty."
Yogesh: "The duck is fine. Teeth, please."
Aadhya: "He wants to swim." (She fills the mug and floats the duck.)
Yogesh: "Aadhya, where's your toothbrush?"
Aadhya: "Um..." (It is on the floor.)
Yogesh: "Let's put the duck to sleep in the cupboard. Then brush."
Aadhya: "Goodnight, duck!"
(She brushes, looking at the closed cupboard.)
Aadhya: "Now story?"

qa.q: Where was the rubber duck?
qa.a: The rubber duck was on the tub's edge.

qa.q: What does Aadhya's saying the duck is thirsty suggest about her mind?
qa.a: It suggests she has become more interested in the duck than in brushing, and the goal of brushing has slipped out of mind playfully.

qa.q: What small step helped Aadhya finish brushing?
qa.a: Putting the duck to sleep in the cupboard took it out of view, so Aadhya could return to brushing.

qa.q: How does Yogesh feel during the bedtime routine?
qa.a: Yogesh seems patient but slightly worn, repeating the request and then finding a playful way to remove the distraction.

grounding: A dialogue shows a young child's attention pulled from brushing her teeth to a nearby toy.

Note from the kindergarten helper, Friday.
Rekha, five, was asked to fetch her water bottle for outdoor play. On the way she stopped to watch the orange fish in the tank. Then she noticed the new puzzle on the low shelf and sat down to try it. When the class lined up, she had no bottle and looked confused when I asked. I walked with her to the bag and let her hold the bottle past the tank. On Monday I will give her one instruction at a time and keep eye contact when I say it.
Seema

qa.q: What did Rekha stop to watch on the way?
qa.a: Rekha stopped at the fish tank and watched the orange fish.

qa.q: What was Rekha feeling when asked about the bottle?
qa.a: She looked confused, as the fish and puzzle had caught her interest and the errand slipped out of mind.

qa.q: What will Seema try on Monday, and why might it help?
qa.a: Giving Rekha one instruction at a time with eye contact, so the goal is clearer and less easily pushed aside by interesting things.

qa.q: How might the other children waiting in line be affected?
qa.a: The class might have to wait a little while Rekha fetches her bottle, which can make lining up slower.

grounding: A caregiver's note shows a child pulled from an errand by each interesting thing she passes.

passage:
Lalit sat on the doorstep to put on his chappals. Kamal dada was waiting at the gate to take him to the field.
One chappal went on. Then Lalit saw a shiny green beetle on the step. He poked it with a straw. It walked. He made a little road of pebbles for it.
"Lalit! Chappals!" Kamal dada called.
Lalit looked at his feet. One chappal. One bare foot. He had forgotten.
Dada walked back, smiling, and held out the other chappal. "Beetle can come too?"
Lalit carried the beetle on a leaf all the way to the field.

qa.q: What did Lalit see on the step?
qa.a: A shiny green beetle.

qa.q: How did Lalit feel when he looked at his feet?
qa.a: Lalit felt surprised, having completely forgotten the second chappal while playing with the beetle.

qa.q: How did Kamal dada help Lalit get back on track?
qa.a: Kamal dada called Lalit, came back smiling and handed over the chappal, gently bringing him back to the goal.

qa.q: How might Kamal dada feel watching Lalit with the beetle?
qa.a: Kamal dada seems amused and patient, smiling rather than scolding.

grounding: Illustrates a young child who starts putting on chappals, notices a beetle and forgets the goal until an adult gently reminds him.
